parts.label: a
hints: Consider finding the total number of unrestricted arrangements and subtracting those where Sam and Toby stand together.
Total arrangements equal 5!, and when Sam and Toby are tied together, there are 4! * 2! arrangements.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the total unrestricted arrangements of the 5 people and the arrangements where Sam and Toby are together:
$$\text{Total} = 5! = 120, \quad \text{Together} = 4! \times 2! = 24 \times 2 = 48$$

Subtract the together arrangements from the total to find the arrangements where they are separated:
$$\text{Separated} = 120 - 48 = 72$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
For two separated items, subtraction is often fastest. Calculate total arrangements and subtract the grouped block:
$$\text{Separated} = 5! - (4! \times 2!)$$

Evaluate the difference to obtain the final count:
$$120 - 48 = 72$$

ai_rubric.observable: Subtract arrangements where Sam and Toby are together from total arrangements: 5! - (4! * 2!) (or use gap method 3! * 4P2).

parts.label: a
hints: First find the total arrangements of AABBCD, then subtract the arrangements where the two Bs are together.
Remember to divide by 2! for repeated As in the total, and treat [BB] as a single unit with the remaining letters.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate total arrangements of AABBCD and arrangements where both letters B are glued together:
$$\text{Total} = \frac{6!}{2!2!} = 180, \quad \text{Together} = \frac{5!}{2!} = 60$$

Subtract the together arrangements from the total:
$$\text{Separated} = 180 - 60 = 120$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the complement principle by subtracting arrangements containing the block [BB] from the total arrangements:
$$\text{Separated} = \frac{6!}{2!2!} - \frac{5!}{2!}$$

Compute the numerical result:
$$180 - 60 = 120$$

ai_rubric.observable: Subtract arrangements with Bs together from total arrangements: (6! / (2! * 2!)) - (5! / 2!) (or gap method (4! / 2!) * 5C2).

parts.label: a
hints: Arrange the 4 teachers first to create gaps around and between them.
With 4 teachers there are 5 available gaps; place the 2 students into 2 of these 5 gaps.

walkthrough.text:
Arrange the 4 teachers first, creating 5 gaps for the students:
$$\text{Ways to arrange teachers} = 4! = 24$$

Place the 2 distinct students into 2 of the 5 available gaps:
$$\text{Total} = 4! \times {}^5P_2 = 24 \times 20 = 480$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Use the standard gap method by positioning the unrestricted group first to form separator spaces:
$$\text{Arrangements of teachers} = 4! = 24, \quad \text{Gaps available} = 4 + 1 = 5$$

Place and order the 2 distinct students into 2 distinct gaps:
$$\text{Total} = 24 \times (5 \times 4) = 480$$

ai_rubric.observable: Arrange 4 teachers (4!) and place 2 students into 5 gaps (5P2 or 5C2 * 2!): 4! * 5P2.

parts.label: a
hints: Because the number of men and women is equal, the row can start with either a man or a woman.
Calculate the arrangements for one pattern (3! * 3!) and multiply by 2 for the two possible patterns.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the two possible alternating gender patterns for 6 seats:
$$\text{Patterns}: \quad \text{MWMWMW} \quad \text{or} \quad \text{WMWMWM} \implies 2 \text{ patterns}$$

Multiply the number of patterns by the permutations of men and women within their assigned seats:
$$\text{Total} = 2 \times 3! \times 3! = 2 \times 6 \times 6 = 72$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Recognize that with equal group sizes, either group can occupy the odd positions, giving two symmetric configurations:
$$\text{Pattern factor} = 2$$

Assign the 3 men to the 3 designated seats and the 3 women to the other 3 seats:
$$\text{Total} = 2 \times 3! \times 3! = 72$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify 2 alternating patterns and multiply by permutations of each group: 2 * 3! * 3!.

parts.label: a
hints: Check whether there are two alternating patterns or only one when group sizes differ by 1.
The boys must take the ends (odd positions), so the only pattern is BGBGBGB.

walkthrough.text:
Since there are 4 boys and 3 girls, the boys must occupy all odd-numbered positions:
$$\text{Pattern}: \quad \text{B G B G B G B} \implies 1 \text{ pattern}$$

Arrange the boys in the 4 boy positions and the girls in the 3 girl positions:
$$\text{Total} = 4! \times 3! = 24 \times 6 = 144$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Because the counts differ by 1, only the larger group can occupy the outer positions to maintain alternation:
$$\text{Valid pattern} = \text{B}_1 \text{G}_1 \text{B}_2 \text{G}_2 \text{B}_3 \text{G}_3 \text{B}_4$$

Evaluate the product of the permutations of each group:
$$\text{Total} = 4! \times 3! = 144$$

ai_rubric.observable: Recognize the single alternating pattern (BGBGBGB) and calculate permutations: 4! * 3!.

parts.label: a
hints: Arrange the distinct letters B, C, D first, which creates 4 gaps.
Place the 4 identical As into these 4 gaps; since all As are identical, each gap gets exactly one A.

walkthrough.text:
Arrange the 3 non-A letters B, C, D, creating 4 available gaps:
$$\text{Arrangements of B, C, D} = 3! = 6, \quad \text{Gaps}: \; \_ \text{ B } \_ \text{ C } \_ \text{ D } \_ \implies 4 \text{ gaps}$$

Place the 4 identical As into the 4 gaps, which gives exactly one way:
$$\text{Total} = 3! \times \binom{4}{4} = 6 \times 1 = 6$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the gap method with identical items. The 3 consonants establish 4 separator positions:
$$\text{Permutations of B, C, D} = 3! = 6$$

All 4 gaps must each receive exactly one A, and the As are indistinguishable:
$$\text{Total} = 6 \times 1 = 6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Arrange B, C, D (3!) and place 4 identical As into the 4 available gaps: 3! * 4C4.

parts.label: a
hints: Position the 5 boys first to determine the number of gaps available for the girls.
With 5 boys, there are 6 gaps; select and arrange 3 of these gaps for the 3 distinct girls.

walkthrough.text:
Arrange the 5 boys first, creating 6 gaps for the girls:
$$\text{Boy arrangements} = 5! = 120, \quad \text{Gaps available} = 5 + 1 = 6$$

Choose and order 3 gaps out of the 6 for the 3 distinct girls:
$$\text{Total} = 5! \times {}^6P_3 = 120 \times (6 \times 5 \times 4) = 120 \times 120 = 14400$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up the boys as anchors to prevent girls from being adjacent:
$$\text{Boys placed} = 5! = 120, \quad \text{Available gaps} = 6$$

Distribute the 3 distinct girls into the 6 gaps in order:
$$\text{Total} = 120 \times {}^6P_3 = 14400$$

ai_rubric.observable: Arrange 5 boys (5!) and multiply by ways to place 3 girls in 6 gaps (6P3): 5! * 6P3.

parts.label: b
hints: Tie the 3 girls together into a single block.
Arrange the 6 units (the block of girls plus the 5 boys) and multiply by the internal arrangements of the girls.

walkthrough.text:
Treat the 3 girls as a single unit [GGG]. There are 6 units to arrange:
$$\text{Units} = [\text{Girls}], \; \text{B}_1, \; \text{B}_2, \; \text{B}_3, \; \text{B}_4, \; \text{B}_5 \implies 6! = 720$$

Multiply by the $3!$ internal permutations of the girls within their block:
$$\text{Total} = 6! \times 3! = 720 \times 6 = 4320$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Use the block method for items required to be together:
$$\text{External units} = 1 + 5 = 6 \implies 6! = 720$$

Multiply by the permutations inside the girl block:
$$\text{Total} = 720 \times 3! = 4320$$

ai_rubric.observable: Treat 3 girls as 1 unit with 5 boys (6!) and multiply by internal arrangements of girls (3!): 6! * 3!.

parts.label: a
hints: Count the total number of letters and identify any repeated letters in SILENCE.
There are 7 letters with the letter E repeated twice, so divide 7! by 2!.

walkthrough.text:
List the letters in SILENCE: S, I, L, E, N, C, E (7 letters with 2 Es):
$$\text{Total arrangements} = \frac{7!}{2!}$$

Calculate the numerical value:
$$\frac{5040}{2} = 2520$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the permutation formula for repeated identical items:
$$\frac{n!}{p!} = \frac{7!}{2!}$$

Evaluate the factorial quotient:
$$\frac{5040}{2} = 2520$$

ai_rubric.observable: Divide 7! by 2! for the two repeated letters E: 7! / 2!.

parts.label: b
hints: You can subtract the arrangements where the two Es are together from the total found in part (a).
When the two Es are glued together as [EE], there are 6 distinct units (S, I, L, N, C, [EE]), which give 6! arrangements.

walkthrough.text:
Find the number of arrangements where both letters E are together by treating [EE] as one item:
$$\text{Units}: \quad \text{S}, \; \text{I}, \; \text{L}, \; \text{N}, \; \text{C}, \; [\text{EE}] \implies 6! = 720$$

Subtract the together arrangements from the total arrangements found in part (a):
$$\text{Separated} = 2520 - 720 = 1800$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Use the complement rule: subtract the arrangements with adjacent Es from the total:
$$\text{Together} = 6! = 720$$

Complete the subtraction:
$$\text{Separated} = 2520 - 720 = 1800$$

ai_rubric.observable: Determine arrangements with Es together as 6! (or arrange the 5 other letters as 5!).
Subtract 6! from total: 2520 - 720 (or use gap method: 5! * 6C2).

parts.label: a
hints: Compare the number of men and women: 5 men and 4 women.
Since the numbers differ by 1, the row must start and end with a man (MWMWMWMWM).
Multiply the permutations of men (5!) by the permutations of women (4!).

walkthrough.text:
Because there are 5 men and 4 women, there is only one alternating pattern:
$$\text{Pattern}: \quad \text{M W M W M W M W M} \implies 1 \text{ pattern}$$

Multiply the permutations of men in the men positions by permutations of women in the women positions:
$$\text{Total} = 5! \times 4! = 120 \times 24 = 2880$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify that the difference in group size dictates a unique alternating structure:
$$\text{Structure} = \text{M}_1 \text{W}_1 \text{M}_2 \text{W}_2 \text{M}_3 \text{W}_3 \text{M}_4 \text{W}_4 \text{M}_5$$

Evaluate the product of group factorials:
$$\text{Total} = 5! \times 4! = 2880$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify single alternating pattern starting and ending with a man, computing 5! * 4!.

parts.label: b
hints: Notice that the numbers of men and women are now equal (5 each).
The row can either begin with a man or begin with a woman, giving 2 possible alternating patterns.
For each pattern, arrange the men in 5! ways and the women in 5! ways, then sum or multiply by 2.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the two possible alternating patterns when group sizes are equal:
$$\text{Pattern 1}: \text{ MWMWMWMWMW}, \quad \text{Pattern 2}: \text{ WMWMWMWMWM} \implies 2 \text{ patterns}$$

For each pattern, place the 5 men in 5! ways and the 5 women in 5! ways:
$$\text{Total} = 2 \times 5! \times 5! = 2 \times 120 \times 120 = 28800$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Establish the binary choice for the initial position in equal-sized alternating groups:
$$\text{Patterns} = 2$$

Compute the full permutation product across both gender groups:
$$\text{Total} = 2 \times (5!)^2 = 2 \times 14400 = 28800$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify that there are 2 mutually exclusive alternating patterns.
Multiply by 5! for men and 5! for women: 2 * 5! * 5!.

parts.label: a
hints: Identify the frequencies of all letters in PARALLEL: 3 Ls, 2 As, 1 P, 1 R, 1 E (8 letters total).
Treat the three Ls as a single block [LLL], which counts as 1 unit.
Count the total units to arrange (6 units, including 2 As) and remember that internal arrangements of identical Ls is just 1.

walkthrough.text:
Treat the 3 identical Ls as one unit [LLL]. The units to arrange are [LLL], P, A, R, A, E:
$$\text{Units} = 6, \quad \text{Repeated letters}: \; 2 \text{ As} \implies \frac{6!}{2!}$$

Calculate the number of arrangements (note that the three identical Ls have only 1 internal arrangement):
$$\text{Total} = \frac{720}{2} = 360$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Group the three identical Ls into a single composite unit alongside the remaining 5 letters:
$$\text{Total external units} = 1 + 5 = 6$$

Divide by 2! for the two identical As; identical Ls yield no additional internal factor:
$$\text{Total} = \frac{6!}{2!} = 360$$

ai_rubric.observable: Treat the three Ls as a single block to give 6 units.
Divide 6! by 2! for the repeated As: 6! / 2!.

parts.label: b
hints: Arrange the 5 letters other than L (P, A, R, A, E) first, remembering there are 2 As.
Find the number of gaps created by these 5 letters: 5 letters create 6 gaps.
Since the 3 letters L are identical, choose 3 gaps out of the 6 using combinations (6C3).

walkthrough.text:
Arrange the 5 other letters (P, A, R, A, E) which include 2 repeated As:
$$\text{Arrangements of non-L letters} = \frac{5!}{2!} = \frac{120}{2} = 60$$

These 5 letters create 6 gaps. Choose 3 gaps for the 3 identical Ls:
$$\text{Total} = 60 \times \binom{6}{3} = 60 \times 20 = 1200$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Position the non-restricted letters first to generate separator gaps:
$$\text{Non-L permutations} = \frac{5!}{2!} = 60, \quad \text{Gaps formed} = 5 + 1 = 6$$

Select 3 gaps for the 3 identical Ls without ordering:
$$\text{Total} = 60 \times \binom{6}{3} = 1200$$

ai_rubric.observable: Arrange the 5 other letters with repetition accounted for: 5! / 2! = 60.
Select 3 gaps out of 6 for the identical letters L: 6C3 = 20.

parts.label: a
hints: Park the 6 cars first to establish the gaps.
The 6 cars create 7 gaps (including both ends).
Place the 3 distinct motorbikes into 3 of the 7 gaps using permutations (7P3).

walkthrough.text:
Arrange the 6 cars first in the parking spaces:
$$\text{Ways to arrange cars} = 6! = 720$$

The 6 cars create 7 possible gaps. Place the 3 distinct motorbikes into 3 of these gaps:
$$\text{Total} = 6! \times {}^7P_3 = 720 \times (7 \times 6 \times 5) = 720 \times 210 = 151200$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set down the 6 cars as dividers to keep motorbikes apart:
$$\text{Car arrangements} = 6! = 720, \quad \text{Gaps} = 7$$

Select and assign 3 ordered gaps for the distinct motorbikes:
$$\text{Total} = 720 \times {}^7P_3 = 151200$$

ai_rubric.observable: Arrange the 6 cars: 6! = 720.
Place 3 distinct motorbikes into 3 of the 7 available gaps: 7P3 = 210.

parts.label: b
hints: If a car must be parked at each end, the two outer gaps cannot be occupied by motorbikes.
Arrange the 6 cars first in 6! ways, which leaves only internal gaps between adjacent cars.
Identify how many internal gaps exist between 6 cars, then place the 3 distinct motorbikes into them.

walkthrough.text:
Since cars must occupy both ends, the motorbikes cannot be placed before the first car or after the last car. The 6 cars are arranged in 6! ways:
$$\text{Ways to arrange cars} = 6! = 720$$

Between the 6 cars there are only 5 internal gaps: C ^ C ^ C ^ C ^ C ^ C. Place the 3 distinct motorbikes into these 5 internal gaps:
$$\text{Total} = 6! \times {}^5P_3 = 720 \times (5 \times 4 \times 3) = 720 \times 60 = 43200$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Enforce the end conditions by excluding the 2 boundary gaps, restricting motorbikes to internal slots:
$$\text{Internal gaps between 6 cars} = 6 - 1 = 5$$

Permute the 6 cars and distribute the 3 distinct motorbikes into the 5 internal gaps:
$$\text{Total} = 6! \times {}^5P_3 = 720 \times 60 = 43200$$

ai_rubric.observable: Arrange 6 cars with ends restricted to cars (6!) and identify that only 5 internal gaps are available.
Place 3 distinct motorbikes into the 5 internal gaps: 5P3 = 60.

parts.label: a
hints: Count the total number of letters and identify all repeated letters in INDIVIDUAL.
The letter frequencies are: 3 Is, 2 Ds, 1 N, 1 V, 1 U, 1 A, 1 L (10 letters total).
Divide 10! by the factorials of the repeated counts (3! for Is and 2! for Ds).

walkthrough.text:
Count the letters in INDIVIDUAL: 10 letters total, with 3 Is and 2 Ds:
$$\text{Total arrangements} = \frac{10!}{3! \, 2!}$$

Calculate the numerical value:
$$\frac{3628800}{6 \times 2} = \frac{3628800}{12} = 302400$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the standard multinomial permutation formula for repeated letters:
$$\frac{n!}{n_1! \, n_2!} = \frac{10!}{3! \, 2!}$$

Carry out the calculation:
$$\frac{3628800}{12} = 302400$$

ai_rubric.observable: Divide 10! by 3! * 2! to account for 3 Is and 2 Ds: 10! / (3! * 2!).

parts.label: b
hints: Remove the 3 letters I and arrange the remaining 7 letters (N, D, V, D, U, A, L) first.
Remember that the remaining 7 letters include 2 repeated letters D, so divide 7! by 2!.
The 7 arranged letters create 8 gaps; choose 3 gaps for the 3 identical letters I.
Because all 3 Is are identical, use combination 8C3 (not permutations).

walkthrough.text:
Arrange the 7 non-I letters (N, D, V, D, U, A, L) which contain 2 Ds:
$$\text{Arrangements of non-I letters} = \frac{7!}{2!} = \frac{5040}{2} = 2520$$

The 7 letters create 8 gaps. Choose 3 gaps for the 3 identical Is:
$$\text{Total} = 2520 \times \binom{8}{3} = 2520 \times 56 = 141120$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Position the 7 consonants and other vowels first, adjusting for the two Ds:
$$\text{Base arrangements} = \frac{7!}{2!} = 2520, \quad \text{Gaps created} = 8$$

Select 3 gaps out of 8 for the identical letters I:
$$\text{Total} = 2520 \times \binom{8}{3} = 141120$$

ai_rubric.observable: Arrange the 7 non-I letters with 2 repeated Ds: 7! / 2! = 2520.
Choose 3 gaps from 8 for the 3 identical Is: 8C3 = 56.

parts.label: c
hints: Combine the block method and the gap method: tie the two letters D into a single block [DD].
The non-I items are now: [DD], N, V, U, A, L. Note that all 6 units are now distinct.
Arrange these 6 units (6! = 720), which creates 7 gaps.
Choose 3 of these 7 gaps for the 3 identical letters I using combinations (7C3).

walkthrough.text:
Treat the two Ds as a single block [DD]. The non-I units to arrange are [DD], N, V, U, A, L (6 distinct units):
$$\text{Arrangements of non-I units} = 6! = 720$$

These 6 units create 7 available gaps. Choose 3 gaps for the 3 identical Is:
$$\text{Total} = 6! \times \binom{7}{3} = 720 \times 35 = 25200$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Fuse the two identical letters D into one block [DD]. The remaining non-I elements form 6 unique units:
$$\text{Base arrangements} = 6! = 720, \quad \text{Gaps available} = 6 + 1 = 7$$

Insert the 3 identical Is into 3 of the 7 gaps:
$$\text{Total} = 720 \times \binom{7}{3} = 25200$$

ai_rubric.observable: Treat [DD] as a single block and arrange the 6 non-I units: 6! = 720.
Choose 3 gaps from the 7 available gaps for the 3 identical Is: 7C3 = 35.

parts.label: a
hints: Use the gap method: place the 7 boys first.
Calculate the permutations of the 7 boys: 7!.
The 7 boys create 8 gaps; place the 3 distinct girls into 3 of these 8 gaps.
Use 8P3 to place and order the 3 distinct girls into the gaps, then multiply by 7!.

walkthrough.text:
Arrange the 7 boys first in the line, creating 8 possible gaps:
$$\text{Boy arrangements} = 7! = 5040, \quad \text{Gaps available} = 7 + 1 = 8$$

Place the 3 distinct girls into 3 of the 8 available gaps:
$$\text{Total} = 7! \times {}^8P_3 = 5040 \times (8 \times 7 \times 6) = 5040 \times 336 = 1693440$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up the 7 boys as barriers to enforce separation between girls:
$$\text{Boy permutations} = 7! = 5040, \quad \text{Gaps} = 8$$

Assign and order the 3 distinct girls into 3 distinct gaps:
$$\text{Total} = 5040 \times {}^8P_3 = 1693440$$

ai_rubric.observable: Arrange the 7 boys: 7! = 5040.
Place 3 distinct girls into 3 of the 8 gaps: 8P3 = 336.

parts.label: b
hints: With a boy at each end, the two outer gaps cannot contain any girls.
Arrange the 7 boys in the line: 7! = 5040.
Identify how many internal gaps exist between the 7 boys: exactly 6 internal gaps.
Place the 3 distinct girls into 3 of the 6 internal gaps using permutations (6P3).

walkthrough.text:
Because boys must occupy both outer ends of the line, girls cannot be placed at the ends. The 7 boys are arranged in 7! ways:
$$\text{Ways to arrange boys} = 7! = 5040$$

There are 6 internal gaps between the 7 boys. Place the 3 distinct girls into these 6 internal gaps:
$$\text{Total} = 7! \times {}^6P_3 = 5040 \times (6 \times 5 \times 4) = 5040 \times 120 = 604800$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Excluding the two end positions restricts the 3 girls strictly to the 6 internal gaps between boys:
$$\text{Internal gaps} = 7 - 1 = 6$$

Permute the boys and distribute the 3 distinct girls into the 6 internal gaps:
$$\text{Total} = 7! \times {}^6P_3 = 5040 \times 120 = 604800$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify that with boys at both ends, only the 6 internal gaps between boys can be used.
Arrange 7 boys (7!) and place 3 girls into 6 internal gaps (6P3): 7! * 6P3.

parts.label: c
hints: Consider the two mutually exclusive end configurations: boy at left end and girl at right end, or girl at left end and boy at right end.
For a fixed end configuration (e.g., boy at left, girl at right), choose which girl is at the right end (3 choices).
Arrange the 7 boys in 7! ways. Notice that the remaining 2 girls cannot be at either end and must go into the 6 internal gaps between boys (6P2).
Calculate the arrangements for one case and multiply by 2 for the two symmetric end configurations.

walkthrough.text:
Divide into two symmetric end cases: Boy on left and Girl on right, or Girl on left and Boy on right:
$$\text{End configurations} = 2 \times (\text{Boy at left, Girl at right})$$

For the configuration with Boy at left and Girl at right, choose which girl stands at the right end (3 choices) and arrange the 7 boys (7! = 5040 ways):
$$\text{Girl at end} \times \text{Boys} = 3 \times 7! = 3 \times 5040 = 15120$$

The remaining 2 girls cannot stand at either end (left end is a boy, right end already has a girl) and cannot be adjacent to the right-end girl. Thus they must occupy 2 of the 6 internal gaps between the boys:
$$\text{Total} = 2 \times [3 \times 7! \times {}^6P_2] = 2 \times [15120 \times 30] = 2 \times 453600 = 907200$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the two symmetric cases of having opposite genders at the two extremities:
$$\text{Total} = 2 \times N(\text{Boy at left, Girl at right})$$

Select one girl for the right end (3 choices) and arrange all 7 boys in the line:
$$\text{Choices} = 3 \times 7! = 15120$$

To keep all girls separated while respecting the end conditions, the remaining 2 girls must occupy 2 of the 6 internal gaps between the boys:
$$\text{Total} = 2 \times (3 \times 7! \times {}^6P_2) = 907200$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify two symmetric end cases (B...G and G...B) and select the end girl (3 choices) with 7 boys arranged (7!).
Place the remaining 2 girls into the 6 internal gaps between boys (6P2) and double for symmetry: 2 * 3 * 7! * 6P2.
